newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX tracks Wall Street to pursue new highs.
newsitem.headline: German DAX tracks Wall Street to pursue new highs.

text.p: German shares surged in early trade on Tuesday, fired by overnight gains on Wall Street to push the blue chip DAX index to fresh records.
At 1015 GMT, the DAX was up 26.24 points at 3,462.31 points, having earlier hit a record intraday high of 3,474.98 and eyeing its next key resistance level at 3,500.

"We will see 3,500 (DAX points), and maybe today," said a Frankfurt dealer, who said he was taken aback by the sheer pace of the market's advance, despite continued solid earnings signals for German firms from the strong dollar.
"If this goes on much longer, we'll be at 4,000," he added.
"There is nothing around to break this momentum," said another dealer. "There is no sign here of a consolidation."
Driving the advance, March DTB DAX futures were up 36 points at 3,464.5 points.

Banking shares were in the spotlight after second tier bank DePfa, a mortgage specialist, issued a statement saying Switzerland UBS had bought up a stake in it in the open market, refuelling long established takeover speculation.
UBS said it had no plans to take over DePfa, but speculative interest pushed the German bank's share up nearly 12 percent, before it settled back to trade up nine percent at 88.10 marks.
DePfa has generally escaped the takeover talk that has propelled German banking stocks to record highs in the last six months.
Other bank shares were also trading heavily.
Deutsche Bank AG was up 1.30 marks at 94.70 marks, after failing to sustain a break above the technically crucial 95-mark level, dealers said.
Commerzbank AG rose 1.01 marks to 45.91 marks and Dresdner Bank was up 73 pfennigs at 57.48 marks.
Meanwhile sports retail group Adidas was up one mark at 168 marks after reporting a rise in its 1996 operating profit on the back of record sales of 4.7 billion marks.
